summary: CKGSB's marketing team is juggling urgent event logistics for the Nov 13 European Chamber Shanghai event while advancing key initiatives like the China Going-Global report, Asia Start (Asia Star), and Intelligent China, alongside a Knowledge website redesign and global search/AI visibility push.
summaryDetail: The most immediate pressure is the Nov 13 European Chamber Shanghai event: registration figures are due early next week from Graeme Wallace, and Shengjia and Graeme must step up targeted outreach to senior executives at member companies. In parallel, the Women in Leadership Forum needs final content pieces—Amber's bio/headshot for Ms. Kanta Singh, Ira and Kaylee's feedback on the warm-up video script, and Julie's approval of the Q3 2026 Business Sentiment Index—while Kaylee sends the approved Sino-Swiss Economic Forum cooperation email. The Knowledge website redesign is moving forward with Joseph sharing the HTML concept and a 30-minute feedback session to lock design changes with Joker, and the global marketing strategy sync has set Asia Start and Intelligent China as top priorities for search/AI visibility, with Joseph tasked to draft target areas/prompts and analyze participant profiles. Looking ahead, the team must launch the Intelligent China webpage, run email campaigns to own and partner networks, and review the Flow website/SEM 2026 report with Gontran once Joseph returns, while also considering Development Reimagined for China-Africa speakers in next year's event planning.

Keep the current Knowledge layout largely as-is rather than a dramatic revamp, with menu categorization as the main change.

Bring BCI and BSI indices into the Knowledge section, similar to the school homepage banner.

Prioritize Asia Star and Intelligent China as top two programs; US partnerships (Stanford, Columbia) on hold initially.
Berkeley program suggested as a possible third priority, to be considered in the audit phase.
